qualitative.gate_3m_moat_note: Patented FcRn antagonist platform (Vyvgart / efgartigimod) enjoys high clinical switching costs and neurologist brand equity in generalized myasthenia gravis (gMG) and CIDP. High orphan pricing ($225k+/year) and rapid commercial adoption generated >$4B in 2025 product sales, swinging GAAP ROIC to >25%. However, long-term persistence faces direct competing FcRn biologics (J&J nipocalimab, UCB rozanolixizumab) and finite patent runway.
qualitative.note: Fails Gate 4 (CAP = 5, REJECT). Single-product commercial biotech relying almost entirely on Vyvgart (>95% of revenues). Under the Mauboussin persistence framework, biotech is Tier 3 (10-15Y baseline), and faces sharp haircuts due to near-term FcRn competition from mega-pharma rivals (J&J nipocalimab, UCB Rystiggo) and primary patent expirations in the early 2030s, capping the Competitive Advantage Period at 5 years (well below the 15-year threshold).
qualitative.evidence: While Vyvgart commercial sales scaled rapidly to $2.2B in 2024 and $4.2B in 2025 generating $1.29B in net profit, argenx's 5-year median GAAP ROIC is -6.1% due to clinical-stage cash burn before 2024. More crucially, revenue is overwhelmingly concentrated in a single molecule whose primary composition-of-matter patents expire around 2031-2033. Aggressive competing FcRn entrants (J&J, UCB, Immunovant) and bio-similar threats prevent confidence in a 15+ year durable competitive advantage period.
